items.title: Beyond static hazard labels: a two-layer temporal object-attribute model of construction accident escalation
items.abstract: Construction safety research often categorises hazards as fixed labels, such as falls, electrocution, or struck-by. This supports reporting but explains little about what makes a condition hazardous and how the condition evolves over time. Accident prevention requires an understanding of how a hazard becomes critical and when worker exposure becomes harmful. This paper develops and demonstrates a two-layer temporal object-attribute model that explains accident escalation as the coupling of worker-independent hazard growth and worker-specific exposure evolution. A hazard is redefined as a worker-independent temporal state of objects, hazardous attributes, relations, controls, and an impact zone. Worker exposure is modelled separately, as the worker’s relation to that state and its impact zone. An accident occurs when a critical hazard state and a harmful exposure state align under actuation conditions. The model is applied through backward reconstruction of 1065 OSHA construction accident reports across six categories: fall, heavy equipment, confined space, electrocution, struck-by falling object, and fire-related explosion. The analysis reconstructs precursor hazard states, exposure configurations, transition mechanisms, and terminal hazard, exposure, and accident states. Escalation was driven mainly by relation change rather than new energy, and the pathway differed by category. Falls and confined spaces escalated through exposure around an already hazardous condition, whereas electrocution, struck-by, and heavy-equipment cases required an explicit change in the hazard state. The paper contributes a temporal object-attribute definition of construction hazards, a two-layer account of escalation through hazard-exposure coupling, and an empirical demonstration of accidents as coupled trajectories.

items.title: Blended learning experience, student engagement, and civic engagement in university physical education with ideological and political education
items.abstract: Objective This study examined how Community of Inquiry (CoI)-based perceived blended learning experience and student learning engagement were associated with civic actions and civic intentions in university physical education incorporating ideological and political education. The study links three forms of learning presence and three dimensions of engagement with behavioral and intentional civic outcome scores in a large multi-site Chinese sample. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 2,035 undergraduate students from 15 universities in Sichuan Province, China. CoI-based perceived blended learning experience was represented by teaching, social, and cognitive presence, and student learning engagement by behavioral, emotional, and cognitive engagement. A 69-item hierarchical structural equation model was estimated using robust maximum likelihood; ordered-indicator WLSMV, Monte Carlo interval estimation, and an equal-loading unmeasured latent method construct were used for sensitivity analyses. Exploratory fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis examined configurations associated with high and non-high civic action and intention scores. Results Under robust maximum likelihood, perceived blended learning experience was positively associated with student learning engagement ( β = 0.530), civic actions ( β = 0.490), and civic intentions ( β = 0.447), while student learning engagement was positively associated with civic actions ( β = 0.375) and civic intentions ( β = 0.396; all p < 0.001). Indirect associations through student learning engagement were significant for civic actions ( β = 0.199) and civic intentions ( β = 0.210), and the conclusions were unchanged under ordered-indicator WLSMV, Monte Carlo interval estimation, and the admissible method-factor model. Civic action and intention factors showed substantial empirical overlap. Exploratory configurational solutions were threshold-sensitive and largely reflected profiles in which many learning-presence and engagement conditions were jointly high or low. Conclusion CoI-based perceived learning experience and student engagement were consistently related to self-reported civic outcomes in this university physical education context. The findings support an associational account centered on coordinated teaching, social, cognitive, and engagement dimensions; the cross-sectional, single-source design does not establish temporal or causal ordering.

items.title: Catch Me If You Can! The Economic Analysis of Geofencing
items.abstract: Geofencing, with the advent of location-based services, enables an advertiser to set a virtual fencing zone around its establishment and inform consumers within the zone to visit it. Yet, when to adopt and how to optimize geofencing remains unclear, despite its popularity across industries. We investigate the optimal geofencing using a game-theoretic model, highlighting the importance of initial consumer awareness in geofencing configurations. We consider an advertiser whose consumers are heterogeneous in location (i.e., local or remote) and awareness level. We first compare geofencing and mass advertising under location-independent awareness (i.e., the ratio of informed and uninformed consumers is consistent in both locations). We show that geofencing outperforms mass advertising as the advertiser focuses on the local market. Two benefits support the advertiser’s localization, namely, profit-margin enhancement and cost savings. We then obtain the optimal fencing radius and price under various market conditions with respect to product valuation and initial awareness. We further extend our location-independent awareness model to a location-dependent awareness, wherein the initial awareness level is negatively associated with the distance to the advertiser. The findings showcase the significant impact of the awareness distribution on the applicability and profitability of geofencing, which is underexplored in the literature. Last, to improve the efficiency of geofencing, we propose flexible geofencing that encourages the advertiser to flexibly choose the point of interest, not always staying with its store location. Our analytics detail the superiority of flexible geofencing over the typical proximity-based practice in the scenario of location-dependent awareness. Such a flexible strategy simultaneously improves the advertiser’s profits, consumer surplus, and social welfare. In sum, we voyage in the ocean of advertising, sail our research to the uncharted treasure island of geofencing, and map a course to take new adventures for future research and practices.

items.title: CDBG: Causally Motivated Dual-Invariance Learning against Topological and Predictive Shifts in EEG Workload Recognition
items.abstract: Generalizing Electroencephalography (EEG)-based mental workload recognition to unseen subjects remains a formidable challenge due to severe inter-subject variability. While functional brain graphs effectively model distributed cognitive dynamics, their inherent subject-specificity induces two coupled distribution shifts: a class-conditional topological shift in the underlying functional connectivity, and a predictive mechanism shift in the learned representation-to-label mapping. Motivated by the subject-induced distribution shifts, we propose CDBG, a Causally motivated Dual-invariance learning framework for Brain Graphs. CDBG disentangles and mitigates these shifts via a two-stage rationale learning pipeline. First, it employs stochastic edge masking to extract sparse, workload-predictive graph rationales, regularized by workload-conditional Laplacian spectral alignment to enforce topological invariance across subjects. Second, it applies subject-wise Invariant Risk Minimization (IRM) to the graph representations, ensuring environment-wise risk stationarity. Extensive experiments on a self-built air traffic controller EEG cognitive workload dataset and multiple public datasets under a strict leave-one-subject-out protocol demonstrate that CDBG significantly outperforms state-of-the-art cross-subject and graph-based baselines, improving the Macro-F1 score by up to 4.23%, while simultaneously providing neurophysiologically interpretable functional rationales.

items.title: Contextual and temporal determinants of injury severity in electric micromobility: a comparative analysis of E-bikes and E-scooters
items.abstract: The rapid adoption of electric micromobility has reshaped urban transport while introducing significant and evolving safety challenges. Despite a growing volume of injury data, existing research has largely examined e-scooters and e-bikes in isolation, and conventional analytical approaches have routinely failed to account for the spatial and temporal structure of injury events. This study provides a comparative analysis of injury patterns and severity determinants among e-scooter and e-bike users in the United States, using 2,413 emergency department cases from the National Electronic Injury Surveillance System for 2021 and 2022. Cases were identified through product-code screening and reproducible narrative-based classification. Injury patterns were examined descriptively, followed by binomial logistic regression incorporating demographic, clinical, behavioral, temporal, and location-context characteristics. Cluster-robust standard errors accounted for dependence within NEISS location groups, while interaction terms examined whether the association between motor-vehicle involvement and severe outcomes varied across injury environments. E-bike users had a higher crude severe-outcome rate than e-scooter users (15.0% vs. 11.2%), although vehicle type was not independently associated with severe outcome after adjustment (OR = 1.071, 95% CI: 0.834–1.374, p = 0.591). Age, diagnosis, body region, drug involvement, and location context were significantly associated with severe outcomes. A significant interaction between location context and motor-vehicle involvement was observed (OR = 2.456, 95% CI: 1.070–5.639, p = 0.034), indicating that the association between motor-vehicle involvement and severe outcome varied across recorded injury environments. Drawing on a Safe Systems perspective, the study argues that effective policy must address the interaction between users, vehicles, and the built environment, prioritizing dedicated infrastructure and conflict reduction with motorized traffic over device-level regulation alone.

items.title: Cross-sectional study on the work-related musculoskeletal disorders among secondary school teachers in Kirkuk City: prevalence, occupational risk factors, and nutritional status
items.abstract: Introduction: Work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSDs) represent a major occupational health concern among teachers globally; however, evidence from Iraq remains limited. This study aimed to estimate the 12-month prevalence of WMSDs and determine the occupational, ergonomic, and nutritional-status-related factors associated with these disorders among secondary school teachers in Kirkuk City. Methods: A cross-sectional descriptive-analytical study was conducted among 352 teachers working in public secondary schools in Kirkuk City. Data were obtained through a structured, self-administered questionnaire assessing socio-demographic characteristics, and anthropometric and nutritional status indicators, occupational and ergonomic factors, musculoskeletal symptoms affecting nine anatomical regions. Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS version 27. Associations were examined using the Mann-Whitney U test, chi-square or Fisher's exact test, and multivariable binary logistic regression. Statistical significance was established at p<0.05. Results: The overall 12-month prevalence of WMSDs was 85.8%. Overall, 67.4% of teachers were overweight or obese. The neck (69.3%), lower back (65.1%), and shoulder (64.8%) were the most frequently affected anatomical regions. Female teachers had a significantly higher prevalence than male teachers (91.0% vs 81.6%, p=0.012). In the adjusted regression model, greater teaching experience (aOR=1.078 per year) and frequent standing during teaching (aOR=4.716) were independently associated with higher odds of WMSDs. In contrast, frequent computer use was associated with reduced odds (aOR = 0.411). Despite the high prevalence of symptoms, only 43.7% of affected teachers sought medical care, and 23.6% had received ergonomic training. Conclusion: WMSDs are highly prevalent among secondary school teachers in Kirkuk City, with women experiencing a disproportionate burden. The findings suggest that cumulative occupational exposure and prolonged standing are important contributors to WMSDs, highlighting the need for improved ergonomic training and occupational health support and integrated health-promotion strategies that also consider nutritional status and healthy body weight within the education sector. items.title: Crypto-bound identity-verified capability tokens for coordinating distributed AI agents: A proposal
items.abstract: The prospect of fully autonomous transactional agents did not appear on the horizon until the advent of high capability language models. With such models, the operational benefits of adaptive task orchestration and independent (but constrained) decision making are tantalizing for enterprises and individuals alike. However, each such agent carries with it a serious attack surface in the form of prompt injection which can compromise any soft "guard rails" that may have been placed in context. The consequences of these attacks include credential ex-filtration which, if left unmitigated, renders the whole category of such agents unusable due to breach of trust. Furthermore, expecting a growth of autonomous agents, a security framework for them would require a form of decentralization to scale. Drawing on the proposed OAuth Agent Authorization Profile and the W3C DID and VC standards, we propose a framework based on the principles of capability based security with decentralized agent identity whereby agents access services based on tokens that are cryptographically bound to the agent's and issuer's identities and specify their scope. Services can validate that the delegation chain only involves scope attenuation before acting on any given token. We show that such a layer that lives outside the language model's context window in a secure module can enable agents to act within enforceable security boundaries.

items.title: Differentiated Coherence in Chinese News Media
items.abstract: This study examines how sociotechnical imaginaries of artificial intelligence (AI) in cultural heritage are organised across institutionally differentiated Chinese news media and reproduced over time. Drawing on nine outlets from 2022–2025, it combines exploratory computational mapping, thematic analysis, relation-focused lexical indicators, independent double coding, and temporal modelling. The primary analysis uses a 232-case high-precision semantic core, checked against a 357-case sensitivity set. The findings identify a recurring normative orientation in which AI is positioned as culturally beneficial through two overlapping configurations: cultural revival and memory infrastructure. Cultural revival is widely shared across analytical positions, whereas memory infrastructure shows the clearest recurrent position-linked differentiation. Public actors are often visible, yet no case meets the strict criterion for explicitly attributed public definitional authority. Temporal tests show persistence in the broader orientation alongside uneven plasticity across articulation modes. The study develops differentiated coherence as a communication-level concept for explaining how a sociotechnical imaginary can remain recognisable through structured selective rearticulation, visibility–authority decoupling, and discursive reproduction without requiring uniform messages or implying causal institutional effects.

items.title: Dosezy: A Local-First, Accessibility-Centric Android System for Medication Scheduling and Reliable Reminder Delivery
items.abstract: Prescription non-adherence among older adults poses substantial health risks and generates preventable healthcare expenditures. Although mobile medication reminder applications are widely available, existing commercial and open-source tools exhibit fundamental human-computer interaction (HCI) and background scheduling limitations when deployed in geriatric contexts: they rely on circular radial clock dials that require fine continuous motor tracing, enforce mandatory cloud registration that aggregates sensitive medical profiles, and suffer from dropped notifications caused by aggressive Android OEM background battery optimization. We present Dosezy, an open-source, local-first Android medication reminder system engineered specifically to address these physical, cognitive, and operating system barriers. Dosezy introduces a stationary 12-Hour Grid Time Picker featuring a 12-first layout and oversized >= 56 dp touch targets, enforces architectural network isolation via manifest privilege minimization through the total omission of the android.permission.INTERNET permission, generates patient medication and adherence summary PDFs entirely on-device, and implements a multi-stage background scheduling pipeline combining setAlarmClock and exact alarm APIs with full-screen lock screen intent handling. We report empirical evaluations across systems and human factors dimensions: Multi-device runtime profiling on flagship and entry-level hardware demonstrating cold startups under 780 ms, vector PDF generation in 142 +- 18 ms, and database query latencies under 12 ms, establishing engineering feasibility against Android 60 fps (16.6 ms) frame budgets. A multi-OEM Doze mode alarm benchmark across five physical devices (99 of 100 scheduled alerts met the prespecified <= 5.0 s criterion under tested deep Doze conditions, 99.0%, 95% Wilson CI [94.55%, 99.82%]). An initial counterbalanced within-subjects laboratory usability study (N=16 older adults, aged 61–76, mean age 68.5 +- 4.8 years) demonstrating a 44.4% reduction in total time-setting latency (19.91 s vs. 35.79 s, p < 0.001), an 80.0% reduction in touch input errors (0.44 vs. 2.19, p < 0.001), and a System Usability Scale (SUS) score of 83.44 +- 9.48 (Grade A, 'Excellent') compared to 57.19 +- 12.45 for standard radial dials. This deposition package includes the complete camera-ready manuscript (PDF and DOCX), LaTeX source, BibTeX database, participant-level usability dataset (N=16), physical multi-OEM Doze mode alarm benchmark dataset (100 physical alarms), and the automated Python reproduction suite.

items.title: Dosezy: A Local-First, Accessibility-Centric Android System for Medication Scheduling and Reliable Reminder Delivery
items.abstract: Prescription non-adherence among older adults poses substantial health risks and generates preventable healthcare expenditures. Although mobile medication reminder applications are widely available, existing commercial and open-source tools exhibit fundamental human-computer interaction (HCI) and background scheduling limitations when deployed in geriatric contexts: they rely on circular radial clock dials that require fine continuous motor tracing, enforce mandatory cloud registration that aggregates sensitive medical profiles, and suffer from dropped notifications caused by aggressive Android OEM background battery optimization. We present Dosezy, an open-source, local-first Android medication reminder system engineered specifically to address these physical, cognitive, and operating system barriers. Dosezy introduces a stationary 12-Hour Grid Time Picker featuring a 12-first layout and oversized >= 56 dp touch targets, enforces architectural network isolation via manifest privilege minimization through the total omission of the android.permission.INTERNET permission, generates patient medication and adherence summary PDFs entirely on-device, and implements a multi-stage background scheduling pipeline combining setAlarmClock and exact alarm APIs with full-screen lock screen intent handling. We report empirical evaluations across systems and human factors dimensions: Multi-device runtime profiling on flagship and entry-level hardware demonstrating cold startups under 780 ms, vector PDF generation in 142 +- 18 ms, and database query latencies under 12 ms, establishing engineering feasibility against Android 60 fps (16.6 ms) frame budgets. A multi-OEM Doze mode alarm benchmark across five physical devices (99 of 100 scheduled alerts met the prespecified <= 5.0 s criterion under tested deep Doze conditions, 99.0%, 95% Wilson CI [94.55%, 99.82%]). An initial counterbalanced within-subjects laboratory usability study (N=16 older adults, aged 61–76, mean age 68.5 +- 4.8 years) demonstrating a 44.4% reduction in total time-setting latency (19.91 s vs. 35.79 s, p < 0.001), an 80.0% reduction in touch input errors (0.44 vs. 2.19, p < 0.001), and a System Usability Scale (SUS) score of 83.44 +- 9.48 (Grade A, 'Excellent') compared to 57.19 +- 12.45 for standard radial dials. This deposition package includes the complete camera-ready manuscript (PDF and DOCX), LaTeX source, BibTeX database, participant-level usability dataset (N=16), physical multi-OEM Doze mode alarm benchmark dataset (100 physical alarms), and the automated Python reproduction suite.

items.title: Effects of Risk Category Levels and Labeling on Non-Expert Hurricane Multi-Hazard Risk Assessment
items.abstract: Effective hurricane risk communication requires risk category systems that support accurate threat perception and appropriate protective action. This study examined how risk category design, varying in the number of risk levels and lowest-category label terminology, influences risk perception, protective actions, and user experience among Florida residents. In a mixed factorial experiment, 368 participants from inland and coastal communities were randomly assigned to one of three risk category designs (between-subjects) and viewed hazard maps for three tropical cyclone scenarios (within-subjects), reporting perceived threat and protective action intentions for each. Results revealed a significant main effect of tropical cyclone scenario on both risk perception and protective actions, and a significant interaction between design and tropical cyclone scenario for risk perception. All designs received favorable usability ratings. These findings suggest that risk category design may shape threat perception under certain tropical cyclone conditions.

items.title: Emotional appraisal in gameful work design: a conceptual framework for divergent employee reactions
items.abstract: Gameful work design is increasingly used to make tasks, feedback, performance systems, and workplace interaction more engaging, yet its consequences remain double-edged. Existing research has largely explained these differences in terms of motivation, technology acceptance, or performance outcomes, offering limited insight into why similar features are interpreted differently across employees and contexts. Drawing on cognitive appraisal theory and a bounded integrative evidence base of 52 publications, this conceptual analysis develops an emotional appraisal framework of gameful work design. The framework analytically distinguishes five interrelated appraisal domains—system characteristics, task design, self-evaluation and identity, social interaction, and organizational meaning—and explains how external design cues acquire supportive or threatening meanings through appraisal. These meanings shape emotional reactions, which may subsequently influence individual, team, and organizational outcomes. Eight propositions translate the framework into domain-focused, cross-pathway, multilevel, and temporal relationships for future testing. By clarifying what employees appraise and how appraisal processes link similar gameful features to divergent consequences, the framework extends cognitive-emotional explanations of work gamification. It provides a focused agenda for future research.

items.title: Empowering teachers for health education: a systemic analysis of engagement in school well-being promotion
items.abstract: Purpose This study investigates the factors influencing primary school teachers' engagement in health education and well-being promotion in France. It aims to identify the personal, institutional and contextual determinants that shape teachers' professional practices and perceptions of health education as part of their educational mission. Design/methodology/approach The study is embedded within the ALLIANCE initiative, a randomized intervention program involving 101 schools across four French departments. Baseline quantitative data from 243 teachers were collected prior to the start of a three-year training program on health education, psychosocial skills and health literacy, designed to support whole-school health promotion. Bivariate and multivariate statistical analyses (logistic and linear regressions) were conducted to identify predictors of engagement, integration and motivation related to health education. Findings Teacher engagement was significantly associated with perceived relevance of health education in professional practice, intrinsic interest, self-efficacy, participation in school-wide well-being initiatives, and awareness of peer practices. Collective dynamics and institutional support emerged as key facilitators, while working alone and lack of alignment between resources and perceived roles were negatively associated. Teachers only motivated by the inclusion of HE in the demonstrated weaker integration, highlighting a tension between institutional legitimacy and professional ownership. Research limitations/implications This study presents several threats to internal validity, including voluntary participation, which may introduce self selection, and reliance on self reported questionnaires, which can generate social desirability and recall bias (Lynagh et al., 1997). External validity is limited by the fact that participating schools were already engaged in a health promotion initiative, restricting generalization beyond similar contexts. Moreover, the analysis is based on cross sectional baseline data, which prevents causal inference; longitudinal follow up and mixed methods analyses are needed, in line with recommendations for complex school health promotion evaluations (Inchley et al., 2007). Practical implications The next phase of this research will analyze, at Year 3 of the Alliance Initiative, the following question: How do the global standards and institutional frameworks promoted by the Alliance for Health-Promoting Schools shape teachers' pedagogical and professional practices in delivering health education and promoting student well-being in school settings? In addition, a separate article will examine the quality of implementation of the Health-Promoting School approach over time, providing insights into fidelity, adaptation, and sustainability of whole-school strategies. These perspectives aim to deepen understanding of systemic factors influencing teacher engagement and to inform evidence-based strategies for embedding health education within whole-school approaches. Social implications The findings underscore the need for targeted professional development that strengthens teachers' intrinsic motivation and self-efficacy through experiential and collaborative formats. School leaders should foster supportive environments that embed health education into strategic planning and encourage peer collaboration. From a societal perspective, empowering teachers to deliver comprehensive health education enhances pupils' health literacy, psychosocial skills, and overall well-being, which are essential for academic success and lifelong health. By promoting whole-school approaches, this research supports public health goals and advances equity in education. Originality/value This study offers a systemic and multi-layered analysis of teacher engagement in health education, extending previous research by integrating personal, relational and organizational dimensions. It provides new insights into the differentiated pathways of engagement and supports the development of whole-school approaches that align policy, training and practice to foster sustainable health promotion in schools.

items.title: Evaluating Transparency Interventions to Reduce AI Over-Trust Among Vulnerable Populations
items.abstract: The increasing availability of general-purpose artificial intelligence (AI) tools, such as ChatGPT, has led many emerging adults (18–25 years) to use these systems for everyday personal concerns. Despite widespread adoption, this practice remains largely unregulated and has outpaced empirical research, raising questions about how users understand and rely on AI-generated information in personal contexts. This project examines how individuals interact with AI when discussing personal topics, such as stress and wellbeing. Specifically, it investigates factors associated with greater reliance on AI-generated responses and whether increasing transparency about how the AI generates its responses (e.g., by showing elements of its reasoning process) promotes more critical and informed use. The findings will contribute to the responsible design of AI systems, particularly for sensitive contexts where users may be more vulnerable and trust in AI-generated information is especially important.

items.title: Everyday AI Use and Career Anxiety Among Hospital Staff: An Exploratory Qualitative Study in a Chinese Tertiary Hospital
items.abstract: This qualitative study examines how hospital staff experience career anxiety while using AI tools in daily work. Based on interviews with 20 physicians, nurses, medical technicians, and administrative staff in a tertiary public hospital, the study finds that AI did not create career anxiety on its own. Rather, it became linked to existing pressures, including workload, patient safety responsibility, performance assessment, career competition, unclear expectations, and limited support. Participants mainly used general-purpose AI tools for drafting, summarizing, information searching, teaching preparation, and research support. These uses reduced some repetitive work while raised concerns about skill gaps, privacy, unreliable outputs, accountability, and possible task replacement. Anxiety varied across roles. Administrative and technical staff were more concerned about automation of standardized tasks, while clinicians emphasized clinical judgment, communication, bedside care, and human responsibility. The findings suggest that hospitals need secure AI platforms, role-specific training, clear accountability rules, privacy protection, and workload-focused support.

items.title: Evolution of Endoscopic Spine Surgery: Contemporary Advances and Future Directions
items.abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Endoscopic spine surgery has evolved from non-visualized percutaneous discectomy only, into a comprehensive minimally invasive surgical platform with expanding indications across cervical, thoracic, and lumbar pathology. This review examines endoscopic spine surgery's historical evolution, summarizes recent advances in technology and clinical application, and evaluates current evidence regarding outcomes, complications, and future directions. RECENT FINDINGS: Endoscopic spine surgery demonstrates clinical outcomes comparable to traditional open and minimally invasive approaches for lumbar disc herniation and spinal stenosis. Advantages of endoscopic approach include reduced tissue disruption, decreased blood loss, shorter hospitalization, expedited recovery, and faster return to work. Emerging applications include endoscopic-assisted fusion procedures, outpatient spine surgery pathways, and revision decompression techniques. Recent meta-analyses additionally suggest comparable outcomes between uniportal and biportal approaches, although differences in visualization, ergonomics, and learning curves remain areas of ongoing investigation. Current data supports the safety and efficacy of endoscopic surgery in appropriately selected patients, particularly for lumbar decompression procedures. Barriers including steep learning curves, limited formalized training pathways, equipment costs, reimbursement challenges, and the need for long-term comparative outcomes data continue to limit widespread adoption. Future integration of robotics, artificial intelligence, navigation technologies, and biologic augmentation may further expand the role of endoscopic spine surgery.

items.title: Evolution of occupational health risks among waste incinerator workers: A four-decade review
items.abstract: This review synthesizes four decades of global research (1980 to 2025) on occupational health risks among workers in municipal, medical, and hazardous waste incineration facilities. It examines how evolving technologies, waste streams, and regulations have shaped exposure patterns and health outcomes. Early studies reported high exposures to dioxins and heavy metals, linked to respiratory illness, skin conditions, and potential cancer risks. While modern emission controls have substantially lowered exposures, especially in high-income countries, residual risks to the respiratory, cardiovascular, and neurological systems persist. Workers in low- and middle-income countries often face exposure levels comparable to those in developed nations during the 1980s and 1990s. Emerging hazards, including brominated flame retardants, per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, and microplastics, add complexity to workplace risk. The review concludes that complete elimination of occupational risk is not a realistic objective and that residual risks require sustained surveillance, updated protections, and global cooperation to safeguard incinerator workers' health.

items.abstract: Mental fatigue is commonly studied using prolonged cognitive tasks, but physiological changes observed in single-group paradigms may also reflect time-on-task, circadian variation, nap deprivation, posture, and cognitive load. This exploratory study characterized continuous heart-rate variability (HRV) dynamics during a 60-min 2-back task performed in the habitual afternoon nap period. Twenty-six healthy graduate students completed pre- and post-task assessments using the mental-fatigue subscale of the Fatigue Self-Assessment Scale (FSAS) and a simple reaction-time test; 22 participants were included in the HRV analysis after four recordings were excluded because insufficient compliance with the required seated protocol resulted in inadequate valid data. Ballistocardiogram signals were acquired using a 1000-Hz fiber-optic sensing cushion. Nineteen HRV features were estimated in 5-min windows with a 1-min step, and temporal dynamics were described using baseline-relative change (Delta) and log change rate (LCR). The FSAS mental-fatigue score increased from 18.99±17.09 to 46.88±24.89 (mean change 27.88, 95% CI 19.34–36.43; paired t(25)=6.72, p<0.001; Cohen’s dz=1.32), and reaction time increased from 371.63±37.74 to 407.62±66.70 ms (mean change 35.98 ms, 95% CI 21.17–50.80; t(25)=5.00, p<0.001; dz=0.98). A BCG-derived respiratory surrogate showed a phase effect for relative respiratory amplitude but not respiratory rate. Across the 19 HRV features included in the primary analysis, several nominal phase effects were observed, but none remained significant after Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction. Exploratory ranking and dynamic time-warping clustering indicated heterogeneous feature trajectories, although the fixed five-cluster solution was not the best-separated solution and participant-level reproducibility was limited. These findings support the feasibility of unobtrusive BCG for describing continuous physiological variation during prolonged cognitive engagement, but they do not establish fatigue-specific HRV phases, diagnostic markers, or individual-level monitoring performance.

items.title: Exploring Generation Z Instructor Pilots’ Perception of Automation: A Preliminary Interview Study
items.abstract: Pilots today learn to fly using aircraft with sophisticated automated systems, such as the G1000. In turn, instructor pilots are faced with the challenge of teaching students how to leverage a system that can affect their performance, both positively and negatively. The purpose of this study was an initial exploration of instructor pilots’ approach to training students on automation, and their perceptions of automation and automation capabilities. Ten Certified Flight Instructors Instrument with an average age of 24 years completed the interview. The key findings from this study include (1) instructors emphasized that students’ manual flying skills will decrease the more they rely on automation and (2) students’ experiences with automation in the flightdeck, either positive or negative, influences their decision for subsequent use. The results of this study highlight a need for professionals to incorporate training and designs that encourage operators to develop an appropriate reliance on automated technology.

items.title: Extended reality visual language for professional contexts: a study on visual dissonance
items.abstract: Abstract Extended Reality (XR) is increasingly deployed in professional workflows, where adoption research has focused on hardware ergonomics and cybersickness. As these barriers are addressed, an open question concerns how such interfaces should be visually designed. Professional XR often inherits the visual register of consumer systems, with saturated palettes, gamified treatments, and stylized characters that may conflict with workplace norms. We define this mismatch as visual dissonance, and professionally aligned designs as native visual language. Established acceptance models capture the social conditioning of adoption through generic normative beliefs, but carry no construct for the visual channel that signals workplace conventions in an immersive medium. This study examines whether visual dissonance undermines perceived credibility across three XR interface components: workspace layouts, avatar representations, and data dashboards. A within-subject survey (N = 96) compared paired aligned and dissonant stimuli with functional content held constant. Sensitivity proves component-specific rather than a single dispositional trait. When asked which variant they would trust professionally, participants selected the aligned one for both avatars and dashboards, at rates that did not differ between these two components, while for workspace layouts the choice was balanced. When each variant was rated separately, only avatars showed a reliable difference: the dashboard effect appears only when a choice is required. Graded self-report alone may underestimate visual effects; XR familiarity amplifies rather than reduces sensitivity. These findings position the visual register of professional XR as a measurable adoption factor to be evaluated component by component and through both measurement channels.

items.title: Extra-Role Behavior in Organizations: A Thematic Synthesis of the Most Cited Studies
items.abstract: Introduction: Although extra-role behavior is widely recognized as a decisive factor in organizational efficiency, current literature remains highly fragmented across disciplines. This fragmentation hinders a cohesive understanding of its antecedents and consequences. To address this gap, this study systematically examines the core themes, relational structures, and accompanying variables present in the foundational literature on extra-role behavior. Method: Following PRISMA guidelines, a qualitative systematic review and thematic synthesis were conducted on the fifty-two most highly cited publications indexed in the Web of Science (WoS) Core Collection. Data collection was carried out between April-May 2026. Results or Findings: Findings reveal that the antecedents and consequences of extra-role behavior cluster into four primary dimensions as leadership dynamics, individual psychological drivers, organizational climate and job design, and negative dynamics. While extra-role behavior flourishes under positive leadership paradigms, job autonomy, and intrinsic psychological states, the findings also reveals a critical dark side. Specifically, excessive formalization and perceived compulsory citizenship suppress voluntary behavioral tendencies and increase employee burnout. Discussion or Conclusion: This research helps to better understand the concept of the extra role by bringing together fragmented findings in the literature. In doing so, it provides decision-makers with actionable strategic insights to encourage voluntary employee behavior.

items.title: From AI Adoption to AI-Augmented Work: How AI-Enabled HRM Shapes Hospitality Employee Well-Being through Job Redesign and Work Autonomy
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly embedded in hospitality organisations, yet research has often concentrated on adoption, acceptance and service-robot reactions rather than on how AI changes the design and experience of work. This study develops an employee-centred model explaining how AI-enabled human resource management (AI-HRM) can influence hospitality employee well-being through AI-enabled job redesign and work autonomy, while examining AI self-efficacy as an individual boundary condition. Drawing on Conservation of Resources theory and the Job Demands?Resources framework, the model proposes a resource-gain pathway in which AI-enabled HRM facilitates redesign of tasks and roles, redesigned work enhances autonomy, and autonomy improves employee well-being. The proposed empirical design uses a three-wave survey of employees in AI-exposed hospitality organisations. For analytical prototyping, an empirical dataset of 450 cases was examined using reliability analysis, descriptive statistics, discriminant-validity diagnostics, regression-based structural paths, 5,000-resample bootstrap mediation and interaction analysis. The prototype results show strong internal consistency and a positive serial indirect pathway from AI-HRM to well-being through job redesign and autonomy. However, the moderation interaction is small and statistically non-significant in the observed data. The study's substantive contribution is to reposition AI-HRM from a technology-adoption question toward a human-centred work-design question.

items.title: Graph attention spatio-temporal graph neural network based human–light interaction modeling for indoor lighting environments
items.abstract: In indoor light environment design, the dynamic interaction between human behavior and lighting systems has an important impact on environmental perception results. However, existing methods are difficult to describe its spatial structure and temporal evolution characteristics at the same time. To this end, this paper constructs a human-light spatio-temporal relationship modeling method based on graph attention spatio-temporal graph neural network, which uniformly represents human body nodes and lamp nodes as spatio-temporal graph structures, and introduces heterogeneous graph attention and adaptive temporal attention mechanisms for joint modeling. The study conducted experimental verification on real indoor scene data for 7 consecutive days and a total of 302,400 time steps. The results show that the proposed model achieves MAE of 0.096 ± 0.010, MSE of 0.017 ± 0.004, RMSE of 0.130 ± 0.015, and R² of 0.943 ± 0.018 in the environment perception prediction task, which is significantly better than various comparison models. At the same time, the environmental perception results show stable and continuous evolution characteristics in the space and time dimensions. Research shows that modeling of human-light spatiotemporal relationships based on graph attention can effectively improve the accuracy and interpretability of indoor light environment perception, and provides important methodological support for intelligent light environment design and human factor-driven control.

items.title: High likelihood of obstructive sleep apnea and associated factors among road freight transport workers in Brazil
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a common sleep disorder associated with cardiometabolic conditions, excessive daytime sleepiness, and an increased risk of traffic accidents. Despite the high occupational vulnerability of road freight transport workers, evidence on the prevalence of high likelihood of OSA and its associated factors in Brazil remains limited. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of high likelihood of OSA and identify its associated factors among male road freight transport workers. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted using a non-probabilistic sample of 597 drivers recruited at gas stations and parking areas in the municipalities of Formosa and Rio Verde, Goiás, Brazil, in 2024. The Berlin-Questionnaire was used to define a high likelihood of OSA. The investigated associated factors included demographic, socioeconomic, behavioral, health-related, and occupational characteristics. Poisson regression with robust variance was applied to examine factors associated with a high likelihood of OSA. Results The prevalence of a high likelihood of OSA was 39.2% (95%CI: 35.3–43.1). After adjustment, high anxiety, psychological distress, and sweets and coffee consumption were associated with a high likelihood of OSA. Drivers engaging in physical activity and those with higher educational attainment had a lower likelihood of having OSA. Conclusion This study found a high prevalence of Berlin Questionnaire-defined high likelihood of OSA among male road transport drivers, which is associated with sociodemographic, behavioral and health-related factors. These findings support the need for targeted screening and occupational health strategies addressing sleep health, obesity, fatigue, and mental health among road freight transport workers.

items.title: Housing and Infrastructure Precarity
items.abstract: In contemporary societies, the interconnections between housing and infrastructure are manifold. Accompanying the shift from feudal to capitalist societies in Europe, infrastructures for water, energy, communication, and mobility were developed within or near housing, enabling the reproduction of labor power. The ideal norm and spatial arrangement of housing-related infrastructure have driven urbanization processes worldwide, shaping expectations of practices (e.g., washing, cooking, and being mobile), while they have been unevenly implemented. Because of the close relationship between infrastructure and housing, a lack of secure housing entails limited infrastructure access, and infrastructural limitations call into question the functioning and stability of housing. This article discusses how the material, economic, and normative aspects of this housing-infrastructure nexus shape housing and infrastructure precarity. It supports recent arguments that housing itself may be understood as a sociotechnical infrastructure, enabling access to systems such as water or energy, forming a base for wage labor in a capitalist economy, and making the fulfillment of social norms, e.g., of cleanliness or privacy, possible. It focuses on housing and infrastructure precarity in the Global North, contributing to emerging scholarship questioning the ubiquity and homogeneity of infrastructure in these regions.

items.title: How can AI accelerate the green transition?
items.abstract: In his essay The Gift, published in 1925, the sociologist Marcel Mauss emphasised the 'total' scope of the phenomenon of gift-and counter-gift-giving, noting that it 'expresses, simultaneously and all at once, all manner of institutions: religious, legal and moral (...)\,; economic (...)\,; not to mention the aesthetic phenomena to which these facts give rise (...).'' The emergence of artificial intelligence (AI), which is suddenly and profoundly disrupting individual and collective lives, bears a resemblance to the ''total social fact'' described a hundred years ago. AI refers to technologies designed to simulate human intelligence, namely an ''automated system that (...) deduces, from received inputs, how to generate output results such as predictions, content, recommendations or decisions that may influence physical or virtual environments.'' 4 (OECD). Having become central to human relations, AI relies on physical and globalised infrastructure and therefore, also has an impact on the environment. This paper analyses some of these effects and how they are perceived by society. This text offers an exploration of the links between AI and the ecological transition, seeking to identify new opportunities and constraints. To this end, it will identify the barriers to the ecological transition (1) and the environmental impacts attributable to AI (2). It will then go on to describe how to live in a constrained world (3) while AI accelerates scientific discovery (4) and profoundly transforms society (5).

items.title: Human Factors in Aircraft Maintenance: Linking Occupational Motivation, Work Alienation, and Flow Experience
items.abstract: Today's aviation maintenance environments place significant cognitive and psychological demands on aircraft maintenance technicians due to increasing fleet size, intense operational pace, and extremely low tolerance for error. In this context, understanding the psychological and motivational processes that shape the human performance of maintenance personnel is critical for the sustainability of flight safety. This study aims to examine the relationships between work alienation, occupational motivation, and work-related flow in aircraft maintenance technicians within a holistic model framework. The research was conducted using data from 207 aircraft maintenance technicians. Descriptive and correlational analyses were performed using IBM SPSS Statistics (version 31). The proposed research model was tested using structural equation modeling (SEM) via the SEM module of Jamovi (version 2.7.6) software and the lavaan package running in the R environment. The mediating role of occupational motivation was evaluated using the bootstrap resampling method. The findings show that work alienation significantly and negatively affects occupational motivation and work-related flow experience; while occupational motivation positively predicts work-related flow. Mediation analyses revealed that occupational motivation plays a partial mediating role in the relationship between work alienation and work-related flow. The results indicate that human performance in maintenance settings should be considered not only from the perspective of technical competence and error management, but also by taking into account motivation and psychological attachment processes.

items.title: Human Factors in Data Preparation
items.abstract: Data preparation is a cornerstone of the data science lifecycle, yet it remains one of the most time-consuming and human-dependent stages. Human factors are critical here, shaping how users interact with tools, perceive data quality, and make trade-offs under uncertainty. At the crossroads of Human–Computer Interaction (HCI), Visualization, and human-in/over-the-loop paradigms, recent research highlights new opportunities to make data preparation more usable, transparent, and trustworthy. Interactive interfaces and visual analytics systems allow users to iteratively refine transformations, explore provenance, and detect anomalies, while cognitive aspects such as workload, bias, and trust determine the reliability of human interventions. Automation increasingly complements these workflows: human-in-the-loop methods leverage user feedback to guide cleaning, labeling, or schema alignment, and over-the-loop frameworks provide oversight mechanisms to prevent over-reliance on automation. At the same time, modern generative AI introduces powerful new capabilities, such as automatically suggesting transformations, synthesizing metadata or documentation, and even generating realistic synthetic datasets. These advances promise efficiency and creativity but raise concerns about reliability, explainability, and provenance, reinforcing the need for careful human oversight. This chapter reviews these possibilities and the research challenges in developing a new class of hybrid, adaptive data-preparation solutions that blend human expertise with automated intelligence. Key challenges include balancing scalability with user effort, ensuring transparency in automated suggestions, preventing loss of situational awareness, and developing evaluation metrics that reflect both human experience and technical accuracy. Addressing these challenges will enable more robust, human-aware data preparation practices across domains.

items.title: Human–AI symbiosis for resilient supply chains: a Delphi-fuzzy cognitive mapping analysis of an Indian textile sector
items.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to explore how artificial intelligence (AI) can augment rather than replace human decision-making in human-centric supply chains, and how this synergy enhances supply chain flexibility (SCF) and supply chain resilience (SCR), using a textile sector in North India as the real-world context. Design/methodology/approach The study is conducted in two phases. The first phase focuses on identifying and prioritizing the relevant AI-related and human-centric factors for the study, which is addressed through an exhaustive literature review for identification and then the Delphi method to prioritize them. The second phase focuses on modeling the relationship between these factors using fuzzy cognitive mapping (FCM) approach. Expert inputs are used to construct the causal structure and analyze the strength of interconnections. By modeling bidirectional and nonlinear relationships rather than assuming static, unidirectional causality, this method captures feedback dynamics, which conventional linear techniques cannot represent. Findings The results show that human-centric factors particularly human–AI augmentation, human–machine collaboration and workforce preparedness play a central role in translating AI capabilities into SCF and SCR. AI-related factors primarily act as drivers, while supply chain outcomes materialize through these human-centric mechanisms. Originality/value This study offers a mechanism-based explanation of AI-enabled supply chain performance and employs FCM to capture complex interrelationships within a sociotechnical system.

items.title: Hybrid Reasoning Systems That Prioritize and Enhance Human Intelligence
items.abstract: In a world of accelerating change, there is a need for wise and adaptive human reasoning. Integrating AI capabilities with human guidance offers promise, though human reasoning itself is often hasty, shortsighted, and error-prone, and no clear framework exists for combining human reasoning strategies with AI across diverse tasks. This article proposes a framework for human-centered hybrid reasoning systems that engage and enhance human reasoning abilities ranging from granular data analysis to high-level reflection and wisdom. The framework was developed through a conceptual synthesis combining: (1) established strategies for enhancing human reasoning, (2) AI design approaches that favor pre-conclusive engagement over the generation of conclusions, and (3) the treatment of reasoning as a collection of distinct, individually supportable modes. This synthesis produced a distinctive framework for broad-spectrum reasoning enhancement from which a typology of reasoning modes, a system architecture, and a high-level research agenda were derived.

items.title: Identifying Workflow Bottlenecks in Virtual Reality Personal Protective Equipment Simulation
items.abstract: Existing personal protective equipment (PPE) research in virtual reality (VR) has primarily examined overall training effectiveness. To inform design optimization, this study identified segment-level interaction hotspots in a CDC-informed head-mounted display VR PPE scenario. Thirty-nine participants completed a six-segment donning and doffing workflow using handheld controllers. Segment completion time and video-coded additional user action (AUA) counts were analyzed using repeated-measures statistics and participant-clustered generalized estimating equations, with negative binomial and mixed-effects sensitivity analyses. Platform or system anomalies were coded and reported separately from AUA counts. Both measures differed significantly across segments. Gloves-and-goggles doffing was the primary combined hotspot, showing the largest time ratio and AUA incidence rate ratio relative to gown donning, whereas goggles donning was the principal donning-specific hotspot. These findings indicate that interaction burden was concentrated in specific segments of the implemented workflow. Segment-aware redesign may improve usability and interaction efficiency in VR PPE systems.

items.title: Impact of Multimedia Display Technologies on Visual Fatigue and Learning Effectiveness
items.abstract: The rapid transition from traditional to digital education has significantly transformed teaching and learning processes. Modern classrooms are now equipped with multimedia technologies such as interactive boards, projectors, and internet-enabled tools, making education more flexible and accessible. However, the excessive use of digital technology has introduced new challenges, particularly digital fatigue among students. Digital fatigue is characterized by mental exhaustion resulting from prolonged screen exposure, repetitive digital content consumption, and limited face-to-face interaction. The increasing reliance on digital platforms has been associated with reduced motivation, lower efficiency, and heightened stress among students. Prolonged screen use can also lead to physiological issues such as headaches, eye irritation, difficulty concentrating, and sleep disturbances, commonly referred to as digital eye strain. In addition to physical effects, digital learning environments contribute to psychological challenges, including anxiety, emotional exhaustion, and burnout, which negatively affect students’ academic performance and overall well-being. Sleep disruption further exacerbates these problems, as excessive screen time interferes with rest and recovery. Moreover, the lack of clear boundaries between academic and personal time in digital settings can result in continuous mental strain. The physical classroom environment also plays a crucial role, as factors such as improper lighting, glare, and poor viewing distances can intensify visual discomfort and fatigue. While multimedia technologies enhance interactivity and accessibility in education, their unregulated use may adversely affect students’ cognitive, visual, and emotional health. Despite the implementation of hybrid learning models, there remains a need for more structured and effective strategies to address digital fatigue. This study highlights the importance of promoting digital well-being through balanced technology use, ergonomic practices, and improved classroom design.

items.title: Incipit: Axiom-Grounded Scaffolding for Human-AI Literary Creation
items.abstract: Large language models can produce fluent prose from short prompts, but direct prompt-to-text interaction gives writers limited access to the assumptions that shape a long narrative. We present Incipit, an implemented research prototype that introduces an explicit planning layer between a writer's intent and generated prose. This layer is grounded in literary axioms, defined as curated and reusable propositions about human experience and narrative craft. The prototype connects a knowledge base of 1455 axioms and 472 typed relationships with a five-round direction dialogue, a retrieval-and-selection pipeline, and a three-level blueprint covering creative premises, story beats and character arcs, and chapter outlines. Writers can inspect and edit these structures before using them as context for scene generation. Additional modules support real-event abstraction and five-dimensional diagnostic feedback. We describe the system design rationale, data flow, implementation boundaries, and a worked design example. As no controlled user study or independently rated output study has yet been completed, we do not claim that the system improves literary quality. Instead, we outline a future preregistered evaluation designed to distinguish the contribution of axiom grounding from that of hierarchical planning. The paper contributes a concrete architecture for using literary knowledge as an inspectable coordination object in human-AI writing.

items.title: Incremental effects of passive stretching added to device-based massage on lower-limb range of motion and neuromuscular response in sedentary adults
items.abstract: Prolonged sitting restricts lower-limb joint mobility, and conventional device-based massage has limited capacity to expand joint range of motion (ROM). This study examined whether adding a passive stretching module to device-based massage produces additional immediate lower-limb improvements. Forty-one sedentary adults were randomly assigned to two groups: the main group completed conventional massage (CON) followed, in a fixed order, by passive-stretch massage (PST), while an independent control group repeated CON twice. The PST phase produced significantly greater immediate incremental ROM gains than repeated CON across hip flexion, abduction, extension and knee flexion. Target-muscle %MVC remained below 5% throughout PST, with iEMG 62-79% lower than CON and subjective ratings indicated positive relaxation, flexibility improvement and willingness to continue use. These immediate, single-session findings offer preliminary support for integrating passive stretching into device-based massage systems; long-term effects and practical application value warrant further investigation.

items.title: Influence of Parenting Styles on Sports Performance among Student-athletes of Lead City University, Ibadan
items.abstract: Sports performance among student-athletes is influenced by their families in addition to their physical, technical and mental abilities. While negative or excessively controlling parenting styles may result in stress and decreased performance, positive parental involvement may promote resilience, self-esteem and commitment. This study investigated the influence of parenting styles on sports performance among student-athletes of Lead City University, Ibadan. Descriptive survey research design was used. The population was all student-athletes of Lead City University (LCU), Ibadan. The sample size was 102 student-athletes with convenience sampling technique. Standardised instruments of the Parenting Style Scale and Sports Performance Perception Scale were modified and used to collect data. The Cronbach's alpha method was used for internal consistency. Reliability coefficients of the instruments were 0.89 and 0.86. Descriptive and inferential statistics were used to analyse the data. The results indicated that there was no significant joint influence of parenting style (F(3,98)=0.935, p>0.05) on sports performance among the student-athletes. There was no significant relative influence of authoritative parenting style (β=0.048, p>0.05), authoritarian parenting style (β=0.156, p>0.05) and permissive parenting style (β=0.014, p>0.05) on sports performance. It was concluded that parenting styles do not significantly influence athletes’ sports performance at this stage; parenting styles may have little impact on their performance, and other factors, such as coaching quality, peer support and personal motivation, are likely more influential. Based on the conclusion, it was recommended that undergraduate athletes should be encouraged to develop self-discipline, intrinsic motivation and personal goal-setting skills.

items.title: Inside the Mind of the Prosumer
items.abstract: Renewable Energy Communities (RECs) represent a promising pathway for citizen engagement in the energy transition, yet their adoption in Poland remains limited despite the nation’s recent individual-driven photovoltaic boom. From a behavioral economics perspective, this Polish experience offers valuable empirical insights for evidence-based green transition policies. This chapter investigates the psychological, social, and systemic factors shaping individuals’ readiness to join RECs. Using mixed methods integrating 30 in-depth stakeholder interviews and a nationwide survey of 974 Polish prosumers, this study provides a multi-level analysis of the challenge. Qualitative analysis reveals how systemic barriers, including legislative instability and deep-seated institutional distrust rooted in Poland’s socio-historical context, translate into individual fears of financial risk and social conflict. Quantitative results show that participation intentions are shaped more by psychological dispositions such as personal values, pro-environmental attitudes, and digital engagement than by traditional socio-demographic factors. These findings underscore that REC adoption is driven by complex subjective motivations and perceived systemic friction that significantly exceeds simple economic rationale. The chapter concludes with strategic implications emphasizing targeted, value-congruent communication strategies and sociotechnical systems designed to build trust and reduce psychological transaction costs. These behavioral insights can inform evidence-based green transition policies that account for the psychological and social dynamics underlying citizen participation in sustainable energy initiatives.

items.title: Inteligencia Artificial con Alma: Modelo Humanista para una Transformación Digital Ética, Confiable y Orientada al Bienestar
items.abstract: Objective: To formulate and substantiate the “Artificial Intelligence with Soul” model as a humanistic framework for governing, designing, adopting, and evaluating artificial intelligence systems in organizations and universities. Methodology: A theoretical-propositional study was conducted through an integrative review of literature on trustworthy artificial intelligence, algorithmic ethics, human-centered design, sociotechnical systems, digital well-being, data justice, explainability, human oversight, and risk management. International regulatory and technical frameworks were compared, including UNESCO’s Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence, the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, and the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act. Results: A multilevel model is proposed comprising six principles—legitimate purpose, dignity and rights, human agency, justice and inclusion, sociotechnical trustworthiness, and sustainable well-being—four governance layers—strategic, organizational, technical, and relational—and a 4A activation cycle: Learning, Attitude, Soul, and Action. The article contributes an assessment matrix, twelve testable propositions, an indicator dashboard, a preliminary 36-item scale, and an implementation roadmap. Conclusions: Responsible AI cannot be reduced to regulatory compliance or technical accuracy. It requires alignment among purpose, data, architecture, decisions, power relations, and human consequences. The model translates ethical principles into verifiable practices and offers a research agenda for validating its usefulness across sectors and cultural contexts.

items.title: Internal and External Factors in Reading Performance Among Grade 1 Learners
items.abstract: This study examines the internal and external factors influencing the reading proficiency of Grade 1 learners at Babag 1 Elementary School in Lapu-Lapu City. Using a descriptive-correlational and causal-comparative research design, data were collected from 100 parents through a researcher-made survey questionnaire measuring socio-economic profile and perceived factors affecting reading proficiency. Results revealed that most parents belong to the lower-middle income bracket, with smartphones as the most available learning device. Teacher-provided reading tasks emerged as the strongest external factor, while decoding skills were the primary internal strength among learners, although motivation for leisure reading remained limited. Most pupils performed at a “Satisfactory” level in reading. Correlation analysis showed that both internal and external factors significantly relate to reading performance; however, regression findings indicated that only internal factors significantly predict reading proficiency. These results highlighted that strengthening young learners’ intrinsic motivation, attention, and engagement in reading is more influential than socio-economic support alone. Lastly, an action plan is crafted and recommended for implementation to foster lifelong reading interest.

items.title: Interpersonal Interaction in AR Mediated Informal Learning on Cultural Relics: The Effects of Goal, Asymmetry, Competition, and Proxemics
items.abstract: Interpersonal interaction is crucial for informal learning on cultural relics. This study investigates how four factors - mutual goals, asymmetric interaction, competitive interaction, and interpersonal distance - affect collaborative learning and collective experience. Through an empirical emperiment (N = 70) analyzing self-report, gaze, and physiological data, the study found that mutual goals, asymmetric interaction and competitive interaction enhanced collective experience, whereas interpersonal distance had minimal impact. Mutual goals reduced psychological stress and common gaze, suggesting that coordination decreased reliance on vision. However, asymmetric and competitive interactions negatively affected learning performance, likely due to the uneven distribution of information and cognitive resource consumption. Close interpersonal distance promoted concentration and emotional stability, but not learning performance. Crucially, findings reveal a structural tension in AR-mediated learning: while interpersonal interaction increased engagement and collaborative satisfaction, they introduce attentional noise that hinders individual deep content processing. The study provides a theoretical and empirical basis for designing collaborative AR systems in the cultural heritage contexts.

items.title: INVESTIGATING EFL STUDENTS’ ENGAGEMENT IN GENAI-BASED COLLABORATIVE INQUIRY FOR DEVELOPING CRITICAL THINKING IN ARGUMENTATIVE WRITING
items.abstract: This study aims to investigate EFL students’ engagement in GenAI-based collaborative inquiry for developing critical thinking in argumentative writing. It employed a descriptive qualitative research design that involved 14 third-semester undergraduate students from the English Education Study Program at STIT Miftahul Midad Lumajang who participated in collaborative argumentative writing tasks supported by GenAI tools. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, classroom observations, and document analysis to examine students’ engagement processes and the role of GenAI in their collaborative writing activities. The findings reveal that students’ engagement is reflected through three interconnected themes, namely cognitive engagement through idea development and critical thinking, social engagement through collaborative interaction, and reflective engagement through AI-mediated feedback. These findings further indicate that GenAI serves as a mediational tool that facilitates not only idea development but also collaborative dialogue and metacognitive awareness. Variations in students’ reliance on AI and their participation patterns highlight the need for pedagogical guidance to ensure meaningful engagement. Overall, the study suggests that integrating GenAI into collaborative inquiry can provide opportunities for students to promote active participation, critical evaluation, and reflective thinking in EFL writing contexts.

items.title: Kajian Antropometri Kaki Perempuan Bandung dengan Profesi Beraktivitas Tinggi dalam Berdiri dan Berjalan
items.abstract: A mismatch between shoe sizes and the foot anthropometric characteristics of Indonesian women can cause discomfort and affect shoe fit, particularly for women whose daily activities involve significant standing and walking. This study aims to identify the foot anthropometric characteristics of women in Bandung who engage in high levels of standing and walking and to analyze how these characteristics align with shoe sizing systems currently on the market. The study employed an anthropometric approach involving direct measurements of 100 Indonesian female respondents aged 18–35 years with high levels of standing and walking activity. Measured dimensions included foot length, foot width, instep circumference, mid-foot height, heel-ankle circumference, ankle circumference, and arch height. Data were analyzed using normality tests, uniformity tests, data adequacy tests, descriptive statistics, and comparative analysis against commercial shoe sizing systems. The results indicate that the respondents' feet had an average length of 24 cm and an average width of 9.13 cm. Comparisons with commercial sizing standards revealed a discrepancy in foot length of 2.49–3.09 cm within the EU size range of 38–42, suggesting a tendency toward over-sizing in commercially available shoes. The "Japan Size 24.0 cm" system most closely matched the respondents' average foot length, although its application would still require adjustments to account for local anthropometric characteristics. Therefore, the development of shoe sizing standards based on the foot anthropometry of Indonesian women and the design of a master shoe last incorporating a 10–15 mm allowance are recommended to produce footwear that is more ergonomic, comfortable, and better suited to user characteristics

items.title: Knowledge of Malaria Transmission, Treatment Adherence, and Antimalarial Drug Resistance Awareness among Adults in Osun State, Nigeria: A Cross-Sectional Study
items.abstract: Malaria remains a major public health burden in Nigeria, driven by biological and modifiable human factors. This study assessed knowledge, attitudes, and perceptions of malaria transmission, treatment, and drug resistance among adults in Osun State, Nigeria, and examined associations between cognitive gaps and preventive/treatment-seeking behaviors using the Health Belief Model. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 1,500 adults (≥18 years) in Osun State between June and August 2023 using a pre-tested questionnaire. Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and multivariable logistic regression were used. Key gaps: 49.5% were unaware of the primary transmission route, and only 27.5% recognized antimalarial drug resistance. Among 712 participants who used antimalarial drugs in the past two weeks, 70.5% completed treatment. Awareness of drug resistance was independently associated with treatment completion (aOR=1.68; 95% CI:1.25–2.25; p<0.001), formal healthcare use (aOR=1.45; 95% CI:1.12–1.88; p=0.005), and lower herbal medicine use (aOR=0.65; 95% CI:0.50–0.85; p=0.002). Female gender predicted insecticide-treated net use (aOR=2.15; 95% CI:1.65–2.80; p<0.001) but was inversely associated with drug resistance awareness (aOR=0.62; 95% CI:0.46–0.83; p=0.001). Knowledge deficits, especially regarding drug resistance, are linked to less favourable preventive and treatment-seeking behaviours. Targeted behavioral change communication, vendor education, and healthcare worker engagement are imperative to improve treatment adherence and curb drug resistance.

items.title: Large Language Models for Test-Enhanced Learning: A Tutorial and Proof of Concept
items.abstract: Practice tests improve retention of studied information and enhance learning and retrieval of new information (test-enhanced learning; TEL). In five preregistered studies (total N = 623)—four online randomized experiments and one correlational classroom study with final-year psychology undergraduates—we examined whether large language models (LLMs; Gemini and ChatGPT) can generate practice tests that promote TEL and whether this use of LLMs can be feasibly incorporated into a classroom setting. LLM-generated multiple-choice tests with fixed feedback did not improve 2-day recall of a TED Talk relative to a control (Studies 1 and 2). In contrast, LLM-generated short-answer tests with personalized feedback significantly improved 7-day recall of an educational video relative to rewatching it (Studies 3 and 4), regardless of whether final test format matched that of the practice test. In the classroom study, participation in fortnightly LLM-generated short-answer tests (with personalized feedback) on lecture content was positively associated with graded assessment performance, and students’ attitudes towards this use of LLMs were generally favorable. Overall, we demonstrate that LLMs can substantially reduce the practical burden of implementing TEL, while maintaining sufficiently good question quality and enabling automated personalized feedback, and that this approach can be feasibly deployed in an undergraduate psychology class.

items.title: Learners’ Environmental Condition and Motivation: Its Relation to Academic Performance
items.abstract: This study investigates the relationship between learners’ environmental conditions, motivation, and academic performance among selected learners during the 1st quarter of the school year 2025–2026. Specifically, it examined the respondents’ demographic profile in terms of age, sex, parents’ occupation, and number of siblings, as well as environmental factors influencing learner motivation, including classroom conditions, availability of learning materials, teacher-student relationships, home study environment, and noise levels and distractions. A descriptive-correlational research design was employed, with a sample of 100 respondents. The findings revealed that learners generally perceived their environment positively, with strong agreement regarding classroom conditions, teacher- student relationships, and home support, while noise and distractions were moderately disruptive. Academic performance was moderate, with the majority of respondents achieving fairly satisfactory to satisfactory grades. Correlation and regression analyses indicated that environmental factors and demographic characteristics were not significantly related to academic performance. The study concluded that while environmental conditions and support systems were important for engagement, other factors, such as intrinsic motivation, self-regulation, and study habits, play a more critical role in academic achievement. The findings suggested a need for a holistic approach that combines environmental improvements with strategies to enhance learners’ personal motivation and learning skills.
